item.title: Herdr's Five Session-State Paths: detach, Snapshot Restore, History Replay, Agent-Native resume, and live handoff
item.description: 'After I close the window / drop SSH / upgrade Herdr / reboot the machine, is my agent still there?' has five different answers. This article takes each Herdr state path apart: live persistence (processes keep running after detach), snapshot restore (layout returns but processes do not, including session-backups recovery copies and the 48 session-snapshots layout copies), pane screen history replay (an experimental feature, off by default), native agent session restore (on by default, with the minimum integration version and resume command for all 18 agents), and live handoff (experimental, opt-in); plus a priority and enablement recommendation for the four paths.

item.title: Herdr Keyboard Control: the Prefix Key, Five Keys to Learn First, copy mode, and a prefix-free Scheme That Does Not Fight Back
item.description: The complete breakdown of Herdr's keyboard layer: why the prefix key exists (the OS, the outer terminal and the program in the pane all claim keystrokes), the five keys worth learning first (prefix+c/v/minus/h-j-k-l/w/q), the full pane/tab/workspace binding table, the editing keys of Herdr's own text fields, copy-mode movement and search rules; the [keys] binding syntax (prefix may be an array, one action may bind several keys, named punctuation, indexed 1..9), the four [[keys.command]] types popup/pane/shell/plugin_action, and the official ctrl+alt prefix-free scheme measured across 10 terminals along with the combinations you must avoid.

item.title: Herdr's Mouse-First Workflow: Create a Workspace and Run Your First Agent Without Touching a Single Binding
item.description: Herdr is mouse-native: click panes/tabs/workspaces to focus, drag split borders to resize, right-click menus to split and create, drag-select to copy, double-click to select a token, Ctrl+click to open links. This article walks the official quick-start order to your first workspace and first agent, marks exactly which actions need the keyboard (only one is genuinely worth learning early: the prefix+g goto picker), and includes real workspace list / agent list output from herdr 0.9.2 on this machine.
